City Council holds hearing on PUBLIC HEARING - Case: 25-0980, Springwood Garden plat

Official Title: 2.B PUBLIC HEARING - Case: 25-0980, Springwood Garden plat | Docket: Olympia • 2026-09-28

For Staff

  • Statutory Constraint Link (Washington Growth Management Act): The matter engages mandate constraints under official state/federal rules (Authorizing state statute (RCW 36.70A: Growth Management Act / SMA) underlying agency administrative action.) which are not cross-referenced in the local staff summary.

For Residents

What Is Happening

The Hearing Examiner is reviewing a preliminary plat application to subdivide 7.2 acres at 1609 Springwood Ave NE into 37 single-family residential lots with wetland mitigation.

The Olympia Hearing Examiner is reviewing a preliminary plat application (Case 25-0980) submitted by applicant AHBL to subdivide 7.2 acres at 7.2 acres, Parcel Number 09680073000. The proposal creates 37 single-family residential homeownership lots along with dedicated stormwater tracts and perimeter open space. The project includes wetland buffer averaging and mitigation sequencing, backed by required performance and maintenance surety bonds.

Principled Analysis

  • Ownership: Verdict: Advances — Enables the creation of 37 fee-simple single-family homeownership lots on 7.2 acres at 1609 Springwood Ave NE, expanding private family housing inventory with required developer-funded infrastructure bonds.
  • Place: Verdict: Mixed — Integrates new residential neighborhood density and wetland buffer mitigation tracts, but requires ongoing monitoring of stormwater drainage and traffic impacts on longstanding adjacent residents.

The Strongest Case for This

The subdivision adds needed family homeownership housing supply on land zoned for residential density, provides dedicated stormwater management and open space tracts, and requires developer performance surety bonds to guarantee completion without public taxpayer expense.

Questions and Possible Actions

  • Authority & Decision Level: State Mandate with Local Policy Flexibility — Under the Washington Growth Management Act (RCW 36.70A.172), local governments are required by state law to designate and protect critical areas using best available science. However, county commissioners hold policy discretion over buffer reduction exceptions and rural agricultural exemptions.

1. Has the applicant posted legally binding surety bonds ensuring ongoing maintenance and replanting for required wetland mitigation areas?

2. Does the stormwater civil engineering plan guarantee that post-construction discharge will not exceed pre-development runoff onto neighboring properties?
